source_text: Quidquid tetigerit altare sanctificabitur. Altare Christus; contactus fidei. Accedite ad lapidem vivum.
orientation: Origen is explaining the Levitical rule that whatever touches the altar becomes holy, applying it to Christ as the living stone whom believers touch by faith.
pass_a_gloss: Whatever [it] will have touched [the] altar [it] will be sanctified. [The] altar [is] Christ; [the] contact [is] of faith. Approach [you all] to [the] stone living.

choices.why: Passive future of sanctifico; the glossary term 'holy' is used for sanctus, and this verb form carries the same root sense of being made holy.
The noun contactus is equated with faith; rendering as a copular phrase preserves the terse explanatory force of the Latin.
Plural imperative; the verb accedo means to approach or draw near, fitting the invitation to believers.
Direct rendering of the biblical phrase; 'living' preserves the adjective's force as applied to Christ.

pass_b_english: Whatever touches the altar will be made holy. The altar is Christ; the contact is of faith. Draw near to the living stone (1 Peter 2:4).

last_rejected.why: Future passive 'will be made holy' misses the force of the Latin future active or middle sense 'will sanctify'—the altar makes holy what touches it, not merely receives holiness.
last_rejected.fix: Whatever touches the altar will sanctify it.
last_rejected.ruling: 'sanctificabitur' is future passive; 'will be made holy' is correct. The -bitur ending is passive, not active or middle.
